title: A Whale Held Its Breath for 3 Hours and 42 Minutes

scenes.text: A whale held its breath for 3 hours and 42 minutes.
A Cuvier's beaked whale, tagged off North Carolina in 2020. One dive. 222 minutes.
The same species dives nearly 3,000 metres down. Deeper than any other mammal on Earth.
That beat the old record by over an hour.
Scientists think it stores oxygen in its muscles and then, when that runs out, keeps going without any, like a sprinter's burn.
Three hours forty two. Now hold your breath and count.

description:
In 2020, a tagged Cuvier's beaked whale off Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, stayed underwater for 222 minutes, 3 hours and 42 minutes, the longest dive ever recorded for a mammal.
The previous record for the species was about 137 minutes. Cuvier's beaked whales also hold the depth record for any mammal, close to 3,000 metres. Researchers at Duke University think the whales rely on huge oxygen stores and a slow metabolism, then switch to oxygen-free metabolism when the stores run out.
How long can you hold your breath? Comment below.
first_comment: A typical foraging dive for these whales is about an hour, and they rest at the surface for only around half an hour before the next one. Which is more impressive: the depth or the time?
